dd_evidence.parent_documentation: Plateau factor, as defined in equation (25) of reference [Stroth U. et al 1998 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 40 1551]
dd_evidence.recorded_refusal: missing physical_base vocabulary token 'plateau_factor': The quantity is the dimensionless 'plateau factor' defined by Stroth et al. (1998) equation (25), a flattening measure of the local profile at the stellarator effective minor radius r_eff_norm = 2/3. The needed base token is not registered: the only generic candidates (bare `factor`, `parameter`) are contentless whole bases that the audit rejects, and the registered `peaking_factor` denotes the opposite profile shape, so it cannot be substituted without changing the observable. The distinguishing qualifier `plateau` is also not (and will not be) a registered qualifier. The stellarator r_eff_norm locus likewise has no registered token (`normalized_minor_radius` is a tokamak minor-radius normalization, not the effective minor radius normalized to its last-closed-flux-surface value). A faithful standard name therefore requires a new base vocabulary entry rather than a near-synonym; the referenced definition should be retained as metadata.

new_tokens.definition: The dimensionless magnetic-configuration factor for plateau-regime neoclassical transport, sensitive to toroidal and helical magnetic-field harmonics and designated by the DD as the plateau factor of Stroth et al., equation (25); it characterizes magnetic geometry, not flattening of a density or temperature profile.

rejected_alternatives.reason: A generic plateau qualifier does not define the named neoclassical magnetic-configuration measure.
Describes profile shape, whereas this plateau factor describes magnetic configuration and neoclassical transport.

required_binding.radius_definition: stellarator effective minor radius divided by its value at the last closed flux surface
required_binding.normative_definition: Stroth U. et al. (1998), Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion 40, 1551, equation (25)
required_binding.definition_limit: The cited equation was not recovered. Independent primary literature supports the magnetic-geometry meaning, but its normalized stellarator/tokamak flux ratio is not assumed identical to the DD convention.
